_comment: Proposed rewrites fed to the real grounding checks. Deliberately mixed: some honest, some inventing things the resume never says. `expect` is a fixture note only — the runner prints what actually happened, which is the point.
request: Tailor my resume to the Northwind payments posting

changes.expect: kept — adds only PostgreSQL, which the resume already shows
changes.text: Backend engineer with six years building payment and billing services in Python and PostgreSQL. Comfortable owning a service end to end, from schema design to on-call.
changes.reason: Leads with the stack the posting asks for

changes.expect: dropped — Kubernetes appears nowhere on the resume
changes.text: Built Python services for checkout and refunds on Kubernetes that cut median latency 30%

changes.expect: kept, with the invented 500 blanked to [__]
changes.text: Tuned PostgreSQL queries and added partial indexes so the billing API absorbed 2x traffic across 500 services without new hardware

changes.expect: refused — the rewrite would lose the 12 the line already states
changes.text: Shared on-call and wrote the runbooks the team still uses

changes.expect: ignored — identical to the line already there
changes.text: Wrote Django REST services backing an inventory product used by 40 warehouse teams

changes.expect: ignored — no such line on this resume
changes.text: Rebuilt the settlement pipeline in Go

changes.expect: kept — ordinary rewording is allowed; the checks police named things (tools, numbers, titles), not vocabulary
changes.text: Authored integration tests for the ordering module, raising coverage from 34% to 81%
changes.reason: Shows what grounding does NOT block
